props.gloss_en: [a deaf-mute, imbecile or minor who slaughtered] among themselves -- exempt from covering
the premise of the stam's question: the Sages do not dispute the first clause (covering), only the last (it and its offspring)
in the first clause, if we said they are obligated to cover, people would say it is a proper slaughter and come to eat from their slaughter
rather, the Sages dispute the whole matter, and they waited for R' Meir until he finished the matter, and then disputed him
(on that reading) the Sages obligate covering when they slaughtered among themselves
granted the Sages: [they rule] to stringency
R' Meir would obligate [one who eats] from their slaughter on account of [eating] a carcass
what is the reason? R' Ami: since most of their acts are bungled
for R' Meir is concerned for the minority
why specify majority? even a minority too: join the minority to the presumption, and the majority is weakened
a child found beside the dough with dough in his hand -- R' Meir declares [the dough] pure
and the Sages declare it impure
because it is the way of a child to handle [things]
R' Meir's reason: most children handle and a minority do not, and this dough stands on its presumption of purity -- join the minority to the presumption, and the majority is weakened
if they said [so for] uncertain impurity, to declare pure, will they say [so for] an uncertain prohibition, to permit?
Rebbi ruled in accordance with R' Meir
and Rebbi ruled in accordance with the Sages
R' Ami: did I not tell you, at the time of the study hall do not stand outside -- perhaps there is someone who needs a teaching and will come to be troubled
R' Zeira: perhaps [the elder] heard it from his father, and his father from R' Yochanan
for R' Chiyya bar Abba would review his learning before R' Yochanan every thirty days
rather, conclude from it: this one [the ruling like R' Meir] is the later. Conclude from it.

supports.gloss_en: דתנן: תינוק שנמצא בצד העיסה... ואמרינן: מאי טעמא דרבי מאיר? ... סמוך מיעוטא לחזקה -- the dough mishna shows R' Meir joins a minority to a presumption (no SupportKind names דתנן)
תא שמע, דשלח רבי אלעזר לגולה: הורה רבי כרבי מאיר. והא כרבנן נמי אורי! -- since he reported only the ruling like R' Meir, though Rebbi also ruled like the Sages, that one is the later

objections.gloss_en: סיפא נמי: since the Sages say it is forbidden to slaughter after them, people will say it is a proper slaughter and come to eat from their slaughter!

answered_by.gloss_en: סיפא, אמרי: בישרא דלא קא מיבעיא ליה -- in the last clause people will say: [he leaves the offspring because] he does not need the meat

objections.gloss_en: רישא נמי, אמרי: לנקר חצירו הוא צריך -- the first clause too: people will say he [covers because he] needs to clean his courtyard (the previous answer's logic, turned against the account)

answered_by.gloss_en: שחט באשפה, מאי איכא למימר? בא לימלך, מאי איכא למימר? -- if he slaughtered on a garbage heap, what is there to say? if he came to consult, what is there to say?

objections.gloss_en: וליטעמיך, סיפא נמי, בא לימלך -- מאי איכא למימר? -- by your reasoning, the last clause too: if he came to consult, what is there to say? (unanswered; the stam abandons the account at 86a.14)
